gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Anker's 10-circuit Home Backup Kit transfer switch fits one F3800 or two F3800 Plus but is 'Not Suitable for Single F3800 Plus', that the F3800 connects to a transfer switch only through its L14-30/14-50 port with the switch's neutral (N) and ground (PE) wires connected, and that the NEMA 14-50 outlet exists on the F3800 but not the F3800 Plus.
standout_why: Compared against Outage Authority (cited), The Watt Guide (TLS error, read via ChatGPT summary only) and the Reliance TF instructions (cited, PDF not text-extractable here). Outage Authority already has the Reliance TF151/TF201 1,875 W / 2,500 W UL 1008 ratings, Goodman's 'properly polarized and grounded' requirement, Mike Sokol's statement that Jackery/Southwire/Bluetti leave neutral unbonded, and EcoFlow's DP3 manual line that a transfer switch is essential. Neither rival gives any maker pairing table for the power-station side: which inlet port to use, which switch fits which unit, and the F3800 vs F3800 Plus port and kit exclusions. Anker's N/PE wiring check is the only maker-written instruction found on the bonding question for any candidate; BLUETTI and EcoFlow bonding statements could not be opened.
decides: Confirms the hardwired-furnace pick stays EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 with EcoFlow's own transfer-switch bundle (maker-matched switch, professional install), and demotes the Anker SOLIX F3800 row: it is sold out, a single F3800 Plus cannot use Anker's 10-circuit kit, and the Plus lacks the 14-50 outlet, so a shopper pairing it with a third-party inlet box must use the L14-30 port. For plug-in furnaces and the Reliance TF151-type single-circuit switch, no maker document opened here confirms any BLUETTI or ALLPOWERS unit as compatible, so those rows should keep 'not verified' for transfer-switch use rather than an implied yes.

findings.label: Transfer-switch kit fit
findings.value: Anker 10-Circuit Manual Transfer Switch (Pro/Tran 2, 120/240 V, 50 A, 12,500 W, UL Listed): 'For F3800 or 2× F3800 Plus'; 'Not Suitable for Single F3800 Plus'
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX Home Backup Kit (10-Circuit Transfer Switch) for F3800
findings.note: Kit: six 15 A 1-pole, one 20 A 2-pole, one 30 A 2-pole circuits, 18-inch flexible conduit, built-in wattage meter. Price showed 'Price Loading', no amount.

findings.label: Connection method to a transfer switch or inlet box
findings.value: 'Connect Anker SOLIX F3800 with the transfer switch via the L14-30/14-50 port, then turn on the AC.' 'Check and ensure the neutral (N) and ground (PE) wires of the inlet box or transfer switch is properly connected.' 'Beware that missing neutral (N) and ground wires may cause appliances damaged on the circuit.'
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX Home Backup Kit (10-Circuit Transfer Switch) for F3800
findings.note: Only maker-written wiring instruction found on the neutral/ground question for any candidate. Anker does not say whether the F3800 bonds neutral to ground internally.

findings.label: Outlet differences and 240 V limit
findings.value: L14-30R: 120/240 V, 25 A max, 6,000 W max; TT-30R: 3,000 W max 120 V; NEMA 14-50 (6,000 W, 240 V) listed only in the F3800 column, not on F3800 Plus; '240V output cannot be used while the device is charging via 120V AC'; 5-year warranty; sold out, no price shown
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus product page
findings.note: AC input listed as L+N+PE; Home Power Panel port L1+L2+N+PE. FAQ lists 'Switching Time: 20 ms' under the wall-outlet condition. The three leftmost 5-20R outlets are the UPS ports.

findings.label: Furnace supply requirement
findings.value: 'Line polarity must be observed when making field connections.' 'The furnace must be electrically grounded in accordance with local codes.' 'Do not use gas piping as an electrical ground.' 'Wiring errors can cause improper and dangerous operation.'
findings.note: Maker copy hosted on ManualsOnline; this page does not mention flame sensing or lockout. Outage Authority already cites Goodman's polarized-and-grounded wording, so this only confirms the rival.

findings.label: What the cited rival already states
findings.value: Reliance Easy/Tran TF151 1,875 W and TF201 2,500 W max, UL 1008, to be installed by 'a licensed electrician or heating contractor'; Reliance Protran2 'doesn't switch the neutral'; Mike Sokol (RV Electricity, Jan 2023) says Jackery, Southwire and Bluetti leave neutral and ground unbonded; EcoFlow DP3 manual says a transfer switch is essential and not to connect without a properly installed isolation switch
findings.source_title: Can a Power Station Run Your Gas Furnace in an Outage? | Outage Authority
findings.note: Rival page notes Reliance's instructions cover portable generators only and do not mention battery stations, and that no station is confirmed to work with any furnace.
